# John Ashdown

- **Role:** clergyman and pastor  <sub>[v5 c5 P128](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0128), [v5 c13 P2](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0002), [v5 c21 P2](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0002), [v5 c33 P22](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0022)</sub>

## Appearance

Beneath his outer appearance, John Ashdown has a mouth that Harriet Ainslie notes makes it impossible for a woman to be misconstrued when speaking to him. When flustered or absorbed in his studies, he has been seen with untidy hair, clad in carpet slippers and a washed-out dressing gown.

_Sources: [v5 c14 P0](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0000), [v5 c21 P12](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0012)_

## Personality

John Ashdown possesses a shy and distant exterior that hides a boyish, sensitive heart. He is remarkably absent-minded and easily absorbed in reading theology or studying, often completely neglecting his meals, sleep, household matters, and pastoral duties when caught up in intellectual inquiries. He is polite, deeply affectionate toward his children, and maintains a reserved, quiet sense of humor, though he suffers from self-doubt regarding his practical capabilities.

_Sources: [v5 c9 P86](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0086), [v5 c13 P2](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0002), [v5 c14 P0](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0000), [v5 c14 P36](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0036), [v5 c14 P37](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0037), [v5 c21 P8](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0008), [v5 c21 P31](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0031)_

## History

Rev. John Ashdown served as the pastor of Glen St. Agnes church, living at the aged gray manse in Juneford with his children and Aunt Martha following the sudden death of his beloved wife Cecilia. Often lost in academic reading and theological dilemmas, he frequently neglected his daily routine and pastoral duties, once even confusing burial rites during a wedding ceremony. During a walk through Fern Hollow, he struck up a deep, intimate friendship with Edmund Carrow and later encountered Clementine Ainslie, whose beauty and maternal nature gradually won his heart. After a harsh confrontation with Mrs. Twiss over his neglect as a father, Ashdown wrestled with his shortcomings and sought counsel from Mrs. Carrow. Eventually realizing his love for Clementine, he proposed to her; however, she sent him a formal rejection, leaving him heartbroken and convinced he could never love another woman. Struggling with his duties, he later agonized over having to discipline his son Rupert, unable to bring himself to carry out the punishment.
